summary: Hiring cooled, oil stayed elevated, and borrowing costs remained near multi-decade highs while stocks traded close to record levels. The combination left markets balancing slower labor demand against persistent price pressure.

markets.name: S&P 500
markets.description: The Standard & Poor’s 500 (S&P 500), a gauge of large U.S. companies, held near a record. Slower hiring supported stocks, while expensive oil and credit continued to pressure company costs.

markets.name: 10-year Treasury yield
markets.description: The 10-year Treasury yield, a benchmark that influences mortgages and business loans, stayed close to a multi-decade high. Borrowers faced costly financing, while savers could receive more income from interest-bearing accounts and newly issued bonds.
markets.gloss: A basis point is one-hundredth of a percentage point.

markets.name: Brent crude oil
markets.description: Brent crude, a global oil-price benchmark, eased after a volatile morning. Oil remained expensive enough to lift transportation and production costs, while energy producers could benefit from higher selling prices.

markets.name: Gold futures
markets.description: Gold futures, contracts for delivery at a later date, moved higher. They can differ from the price of gold available for immediate delivery, known as the spot price.

markets.name: U.S. Dollar Index
markets.description: The U.S. Dollar Index (DXY), which compares the dollar with major currencies, strengthened. Importers and travelers abroad can benefit from a firmer dollar, while U.S. exporters may find their products costlier overseas.

markets.name: Expected volatility
markets.description: The Cboe Volatility Index (VIX), a measure of expected stock-market swings, moved higher. The increase showed stronger demand for protection, though the level remained below periods of severe market stress.

calendar.title: Consumer Price Index (CPI)
calendar.definition: A measure of price changes for goods and services purchased by households.
calendar.hot: A higher-than-expected reading has often been associated with greater interest-rate pressure.
calendar.cool: A lower-than-expected reading has often been associated with less interest-rate pressure.

calendar.title: Producer Price Index (PPI)
calendar.definition: A measure of price changes received by domestic producers before many costs reach consumers.
calendar.hot: A higher-than-expected reading has often been associated with concern about future consumer-price pressure.
calendar.cool: A lower-than-expected reading has often been associated with easing business-cost pressure.

calendar.time: Decision at 2:00 p.m. ET on Oct. 28
calendar.title: Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting
calendar.definition: The Federal Reserve group that sets the target range for short-term interest rates.
calendar.hot: A tighter decision has often been associated with higher short-term borrowing costs.
calendar.cool: An unchanged rate has often been associated with more time for officials to assess inflation and employment.
